related_questions.question: What are the four types of subunit vaccines?
related_questions.snippet: Subunit, recombinant, polysaccharide, and conjugate vaccines use specific pieces of the germ—like its protein, sugar, or capsid (a casing around the germ). Because these vaccines use only specific pieces of the germ, they give a very strong immune response that's targeted to key parts of the germ.

related_questions.question: What are the disadvantages of subunit vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: Subunit vaccines, which use specific pieces of a pathogen to trigger an immune response, can have several disadvantages. They may require adjuvants to boost their effectiveness, necessitating multiple doses for adequate protection, and might not provide the broad coverage of whole-pathogen vaccines. Additionally, they can be more expensive to produce due to the need for specialized equipment and processes to isolate and purify the antigens.
snippet_highlighted_words: They may require adjuvants to boost their effectiveness, necessitating multiple doses for adequate protection, and might not provide the broad coverage of whole-pathogen vaccines

list.title: Lower Immunogenicity:
list.snippet: Subunit vaccines often trigger a weaker immune response compared to whole-pathogen vaccines. This is because they lack the full range of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that stimulate a more robust immune response.

list.title: Need for Adjuvants:
list.snippet: To compensate for the lower immunogenicity, subunit vaccines frequently require adjuvants, which are substances that enhance the vaccine's ability to stimulate the immune system.

list.title: Multiple Doses:
list.snippet: Due to the weaker immune response, subunit vaccines often require multiple doses (boosters) to achieve and maintain adequate protection.

list.title: Limited Coverage:
list.snippet: Because they only contain specific antigens, subunit vaccines may not provide the same broad protection as whole-pathogen vaccines, which expose the immune system to a wider range of pathogen components.

list.title: Higher Production Costs:
list.snippet: While the production process for subunit vaccines can be relatively simple, the extraction and purification of high-quality antigen proteins can be expensive and require specialized equipment, potentially leading to higher production costs.

related_questions.question: What is the difference between a whole vaccine and a subunit vaccine?
related_questions.snippet: Whole-cell vaccines contain an inactivated version of the entire pathogen (virus or bacteria). Subunit vaccines include only parts of the virus or bacteria that contain the antigens needed to stimulate an immune response, but do not include all the other molecules in the virus or bacteria.
